children: Long before
Neal Mohan
YouTube’s
CEO, a sold-out screening of "Star Wars" gave the future tech executive an early glimpse of the world that would eventually shape his career.
Neal Mohan’s Childhood ‘Star Wars’ Obsession
In 2023, Mohan, MBA ’05, returned to Stanford for the View From The Top speaker series, where he spoke with Shannon Beckham, MBA ’24, about his childhood.
Reflecting on growing up in the early 1980s, Mohan called it a "pretty normal childhood" filled with Transformers, Star Wars and baseball.
According to TIME’s 2025 profile of Mohan, the YouTube chief was just 6 when he convinced his parents to drive to Ann Arbor, Michigan,
When they discovered the movie was sold out, he persuaded them to make the trip again the following night.
"That movie changed my life," Mohan told the magazine.
The experience became more than a childhood memory. Mohan still keeps a Yoda figurine on his desk that his mother gave him.

children: From America to India
Mohan’s childhood took another dramatic turn in the mid-1980s when his parents moved him and his two brothers to Lucknow, India, when he was 12.
The transition was difficult. Mohan had to adjust to leaving his friends behind while learning to speak and read Hindi and studying Sanskrit.
He later compared Sanskrit’s highly structured and phonetic nature to computer programming, calling it "incredibly phonetic and rules-oriented," the magazine noted.
"It’s really about not just surviving. It’s about thriving through those types of kind of seminal, sort of pivotal moments," he told Beckham.
His family also encouraged taking risks. Mohan’s father had moved to the U.S. from India in the 1960s to pursue a Ph.D. at
Purdue University
, arriving with just $25.
Neal Mohan’s Path to Google and YouTube
After studying at Stanford, Mohan began his career in consulting before joining internet advertising startup
NetGravity
. The company was later acquired by
DoubleClick
Google
agreed to acquire DoubleClick for $3.1 billion, a deal that strengthened its display advertising business.
DoubleClick had also faced scrutiny over its use of cookies and online tracking technology.
Mohan eventually rose through Google’s ranks
Susan Wojcicki
as YouTube CEO in 2023. TIME named him its 2025 CEO of the Year.
